findings.cited_line: - **Step 7: Wait for convergence.** Barrier pattern: wait for all N workers OR `timeout_ms` (15 min default; Figma MCP latency can be high). Read all `.partial.json` files in `active/<task>/.wos/fleet-inbox/<run_id>/`. Classify per `commands/_shared/convergence-policy.md` failure table. Workers that did not invoke StructuredOutput (schema-skip) are classified `failed` and excluded from merge.
findings.defect: ADR-0158 D-1 accepts a worker-written fleet-inbox/<run_id>/<worker_id>.json on the Agent path and a runtime-driven typed result on the dynamic-workflow path; D-2 limits the new write exception to that run inbox. The cited command-owned rule nevertheless classifies a worker as failed solely for not invoking StructuredOutput. A worker that obeys the accepted Agent carrier therefore fails this test even with a valid payload. This is one family defect, not seven independent findings: every fleet dispatch still says that the Agent worker returns text and the orchestrator persists it; implement-fleet and task-init-fleet additionally tell the worker to invoke the unavailable tool, screen-spec-fleet and verify-against-rubric-fleet retain tool-only worker/reader/DoD rules, and both research fleets have path-aware dispatch text contradicted by tool-only completion rules. Permission wording also has to agree: atom-audit-fleet forbids every substrate write; implement-fleet forbids every write outside scope_files; verify-against-rubric-fleet promises only read-only tools and excludes return-address metadata from its ONLY input list. These statements do not accommodate the already-authorized inbox file without an explicit narrow qualification. The current spec's Per-batch checklist requires a typed-return reminder whose carrier depends on the dispatch path. This is a correction to the existing policy, not a request for a new transport or broader worker access.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the command-owned return contract together at all seven sites. Keep the existing worker_input_schema and worker_output_schema unchanged. Name the dispatch path before dispatch; supply the existing worker-contract envelope's fleet_inbox_artifact as a resolved per-worker .json path within this run's existing .wos/fleet-inbox/<run_id>/ location, outside task_input. On Agent, instruct the worker to write the one schema-conforming JSON payload to that path and the orchestrator to read it. On dynamic-workflow, declare agent(prompt, {schema}) and consume the runtime's typed result; never tell the worker to call StructuredOutput or supply an artifact= API parameter. Replace the stale Agent-text/orchestrator-persistence tail instead of appending another contradictory rule. Make worker templates and final reminders, convergence readers, output-path descriptions, DoD and quality-bar statements agree with the selected carrier; determine schema-skip from a missing or invalid payload on that carrier, not from absence of a worker tool invocation. Preserve each command's existing status/error fields, failure classifications/events, retry limits, partial_ok, merge keys, barriers, and refusal routes. Distinguish canonical Agent .json from optional orchestrator replay .partial.json; readers must not ignore the canonical file or double-count its replay. Qualify atom-audit-fleet's blanket write ban and implement-fleet's scope restriction with only the assigned return file; retain implement-fleet's existing slice-note and scoped worktree writes, screen-spec-fleet's own spec-file writes, and task-init-fleet's own task-folder writes. Keep all shared canonical artifacts owned by their existing orchestrator. In verify-against-rubric-fleet, qualify the description, Step 5 and DoD isolation wording to permit only the required artifact identifier/schema and delivery metadata plus the assigned return-file write; artifacts, rubric and sibling/task-history exclusions remain read-only and isolated. No new outputs or payload fields are needed. For implement-fleet Step 8, select its already-permitted inbox polling alternative for the flat JSON return: scripts/monitor-fleet-progress.sh currently reads <worker_id>/status and terminal.json subdirectories, so do not claim that unadapted script observes flat <worker_id>.json payloads. Keep the existing visibility and timeout duties. Required dependent edits: update templates/ORCHESTRATOR_COMMAND.template.md's dispatch, YAML-header/body reader and blanket worker-write language to the same JSON carrier contract; update evals/scenarios/39-workflow-prompt-too-long-ci.md's safe reminder fixture, evals/scenarios/40-fleet-command-adr0038-compliance.md's exact tool-call/write-ban requirements, and evals/scenarios/59-feature-library-scout.md's fleet expectation so valid results through either carrier pass and prose/missing/invalid returns still fail; synchronize the affected evals/README.md summaries. Update live carrier/ownership guidance in wos/substrate-peers.md (matrix legend, Epic J fleet workers, Pattern C) and wos/sub-agent-orchestration.md (dispatch guidance and schema-skip/reminder descriptions); qualify the current reusable guidance/examples in wos/workflow-patterns.md and wos/bug-classes/{workflow-prompt-too-long,schema-skip-on-structured-output}.md so they cannot reinstate a worker-side tool mandate. Preserve historical measurements and ADR Decision bodies. Preserve the literal 'Name the path you are on' in corrected command-owned dispatch instructions because evals/scripts/structural-evals.py check_structured_output_names_its_path currently uses that sentinel, and introduce no artifact= mandate. Shared blocks and their source files remain out of scope and unchanged. After a separately authorized implementation, regenerate skills with scripts/build-agent-skills.sh and run scripts/lint-commands.sh plus evals/scripts/structural-evals.py; the positive acceptance cases must include a valid Agent file and a valid runtime result, without changing schema/status/merge behavior. This audit applies no source edit; chars_delta is 0.
